what: The mechanical definition of the gates of the Urazuke method, published as data. The method owns it; a tool consumes it. Whatever an installation cannot measure is reported as declared and not measured, never as green.

content_hash.note: Recompute it over the canonicalised payload and compare. If you only read it, a frozen copy edited by hand or truncated by a merge is undetectable.

git_commit_note: Informative. It is the sha of the change BEFORE the one that contains this file, because it is computed before saving: it is not the identity of what is published and no comparison looks at it.

languages.note: The prose of the method (docs/) is written in Spanish and translated into seven more languages. The data layer (gates/ and the published file) is written in English, which is the canonical language of the profession, because it is not part of the translated corpus. Translating for the comprehension of an end user is the job of the consumer tool, not of this catalogue.
languages.exception: The frozen base (gates/baseline.json) keeps the Spanish text and the `tramo` field name it had when the method took ownership. The base is not edited: changing it is a change of the method, with its own decision.

text_language.what: Which language each human-readable text of this file is in. It is declared mechanically because the file is bilingual: reading `data` as a single language would make a consumer show Spanish to an English reader.
text_language.rule: Inside the keys listed in `spanish_scope`, a text is Spanish when neither its own node nor any enclosing node declares `since_schema` >= 2: it comes from the frozen base, and the base is not edited. A node with `since_schema` >= 2 is new, and its text is English. Every text outside `spanish_scope` is English.
text_language.language_neutral: Ids, step and station keys, evaluator names, enum values, file paths and the regular expressions of must_contain / should_contain are not prose and carry no language. The regular expressions are deliberately bilingual, so that a gate matches a document written in either language.
text_language.verified: The method checks this declaration on every build: every text the rule calls Spanish has to appear literally in gates/baseline.json, and no text the rule calls English may read as Spanish. If the declaration stops being true, nothing is published.
text_language.consumer: Do not print these texts to an end user. Read the stable `id` -- an opaque key that is never translated -- and take the text from your own catalogue. That holds for the English texts too: this file is the definition of the gates, not a translated user interface.

evaluators.name: artifacts
evaluators.checks: Every declared artifact exists, passes its min_bytes, satisfies each must_contain and, if it is a glob, the newest one is within its fresh_days. A should_contain that does not appear leaves a warning, not a red.

evaluators.name: sizing
evaluators.checks: The artifacts, plus an admissible sizing record: volumetry, retention per data class and hardware envelope, all declared by the owner.

evaluators.name: ci
evaluators.checks: The artifacts, plus a continuous integration definition that exists in the repository.

evaluators.name: pendings_spec
evaluators.checks: The artifacts, plus every open pending item carrying its full specification (acceptance criteria and how it is verified). An empty plan is red, not green.

evaluators.name: receipts
evaluators.checks: The artifacts, plus evidence receipts including at least one proven red and one green. No receipt, no step.

evaluators.name: reports
evaluators.checks: The artifacts, plus every closed pending item having its honest report (verified / believed / blind spot). No closure yet is red, not green.

evaluators.name: meters
evaluators.checks: A meter exists in the repository and the meter has a test of its own.

evaluators.name: owner
evaluators.checks: Nothing mechanical: the owner verifies it and signs it. No step of the catalogue chooses it today; the state exists for a step that leaves no machine check at all, and that is why the name is published anyway.

evaluators.name: heuristics
evaluators.checks: The Annex H rule catalogue is declared and active per group; every active rule has an instrument, a severity and a checker; every switched-off rule has its record with reason, author and review date (switched off without a record is red, not the absence of a rule); every undeclared threshold is reported as undeclared instead of invented; and the report emits the two figures with the ruleset fingerprint. A switched-off group is never read as fulfilled.

evaluators.name: profile_matrix
evaluators.checks: The functionality-by-profile matrix exists and is consistent: every functionality has at least one profile, every profile has at least one functionality and its entry point, and navigation is derived from the matrix rather than hand-written. And for every profile, the end-to-end test compares what is reachable against its row: neither less nor more.

evaluators.name: manual_cases_per_profile
evaluators.checks: Every manual test case was run once per affected profile, derived from the matrix. A case run with a single profile does not count as executed.

evaluators.name: pendings_profiles
evaluators.checks: Every pending item that touches a screen declares its functional convergence group, the profiles that have it and one acceptance criterion per profile. Without that declaration the pending item does not pass the step.

evaluator_semantics.required_true: A step that declares this evaluator needs the installation to know how to measure it. An installation that does not know it does NOT report green: it reports "declared, not measured by this installation" and the step does not advance. No approximating with the closest evaluator, and no ignoring.
evaluator_semantics.required_false: A warning, not a gate: an installation that does not know it says so and the step may advance anyway.
evaluator_semantics.unknown_name: A name that is not in this list is a catalogue error, not an extension: the validator rejects it.

compatibility.unknown_evaluator_required: The installation does NOT report green. It reports "declared, not measured by this installation", naming the evaluator, and the step does not advance.
compatibility.unknown_evaluator_not_required: A warning: it names it and the step may advance.
compatibility.forbidden: Approximating with the closest evaluator, or ignoring the block. Zero silent damage.

loop_entry.note: A legacy system enters the Construction Loop at step 5, so from there the five anchors of Annex H rule exactly as they do in a new project (D-023 + D-043). The two prior inputs are recovered by self-discovery with a source mark, like every input of an earlier stage on this path.

heuristics.what: The forty-five rules of Annex H as data: 18 of code quality (CQ-01 to CQ-18) and 27 of usability (UX-01 to UX-27). The mechanical fields live here. The STATEMENT of every rule lives ONLY in Annex H: this file carries the pointer and the build extracts the text (D-044). Ids are append-only.

severities.blocks: the gate goes red and the block does not close
severities.warns: it opens a pending item naming the rule and the file; warning is not approving
severities.records: it only stays in the document

switch_off.without_record: red: switching a rule off without a written reason is a failure of the gate, not the absence of a rule
switch_off.with_record: green, and the report says it is switched off, since when and who authorised it

instruments.returns: passed or failed, with a name and a date

prior_inputs.without_it: UX-01 and UX-24 have nothing to compare against
prior_inputs.note: The annex requires it when scope is defined and declares no file for it. Since 2026-10-26 the step 2 contract DOES ask for it, in writing and named from the project file, and the step 2 completeness check reads it; what the method still does not declare is a canonical path, on purpose, because the owner never declared one and a file name invented here would be published as a default. So it stays machine-measurable only through the step 2 checklist: declared, and not measured by path.

prior_inputs.without_it: the B2 matrix gets invented at step 5
prior_inputs.note: Same status as prior input 1: asked for by the step 2 contract since 2026-10-26, with no canonical path declared.

anchors.what: every pending item that touches a screen declares its convergence group, its profiles and acceptance criteria per profile
the matrix as a test that is seen failing first
the full CQ catalogue with its adapter and declared thresholds, and the matrix as a gate
one manual case per affected profile, derived from the matrix
the report says what was measured, what was left warning and which rule is switched off, with reason, author and review date

artifacts.what: the result per code-quality rule, not a single number
the result per usability rule and the declared exceptions
the matrix: a document and the source of the menu at the same time

figures.moves: goes up when something is fixed
goes down when a rule is switched off

statement_source.single_copy: The statement of every rule lives only in Annex H (D-044). The build extracts it from the English version, which is the one published; the Spanish version is the source of truth of the method and the build checks both carry the same rules with the same severities.
statement_source.not_measured: Whether the English wording still says what the Spanish one says is not checked by machine: only the set of rules and their severities are.

statement.text: There is a single formatter, it runs without intervention and it admits no discussion.
There is a single linter per repository and its rules are the same for everybody; a rule is switched off with a written reason, never in a loose file.
No file exceeds the declared limit (starts at 300 lines) and no function exceeds its own (starts at 40).
No function exceeds the declared path limit.
No new duplication enters: the copied block is extracted or justified.
There is no dead code: unused functions, variables, imports, branches and dependencies.
If the language allows types, the project uses them seriously; the "any" type is a declared exception, not a habit.
Coverage does not go down: today's number is tomorrow's floor.
With real users, the mutation score is measured per block and every mutant that survives in new code opens a pending item.

rules.requires_record: a score per block, and every surviving mutant in new code opens a pending item

statement.text: Every dependency is declared, is used and does not bring a third-party tree out of proportion to what it contributes.
There are no credentials, keys or connection strings in the repository, nor in the new history.
The interface does not decide: no screen or component contains business rules (what is allowed, how much it costs, which state follows). It lives in the domain and the view queries it.
Every server call goes through a single typed client; no screen builds its own request by hand.
There is a single place where shared state lives; duplicating state between screens is a failure, not a shortcut.
Every visible text comes out of a translation catalogue; no user string stays written inside the component.
Every interactive element carries a stable identifier and a role, so that the automated test finds it by name and not by position.
All colours, spacings and typefaces come out of tokens; no loose magic value in the stylesheet.
Basic accessibility is verified on its own: contrast, labels on fields, visible focus, keyboard navigation in the main flows, images with alternative text.

escalates_to.when: the product has end users outside the organisation
escalates_to.requires: a declaration by the owner, through the same mechanism as any threshold

statement.text: Every menu group is named with a user job (in their vocabulary, with the project glossary), never with a technical module nor with a data entity.
Every functionality has exactly one canonical home. If it serves two groups, one home is chosen and the other links to it; the entry is not duplicated.
There are no orphans: every declared functionality is reachable from the entry screen in no more than three steps.
The size of a group is reasonable: fewer than three functionalities indicates a group that was not a group; more than seven indicates a drawer.
Every group has an entry screen that says what is done there and which is the main action. No group opens straight into an empty table.
The flows the person does often live together: if "record a payment" and "see the customer's account" are used in the same session, they share a group.

The first-click test: the owner, facing a concrete task ("where do you charge a payment?"), names one place. If they name two, there is duplication; if they name none, there is an orphan. It runs at the close of every block.
Every functionality declares in the matrix which profiles have it. A functionality without a profile does not exist: either it is given a profile or it is deleted.
Every declared profile has at least one functionality and its own entry point. An empty profile is a profile nobody used while designing.
Navigation is generated from the matrix. A hand-written menu is a failure, not a shortcut.
Hiding is not protecting: every route verifies the permission on the server side in addition to hiding the entry. Typing the address by hand is not enough to get in.
Neither less nor more: for each profile, the set of reachable functionalities is exactly the one in its row of the matrix.

The refusal is explained: if a person enters a functionality that is not theirs, they see a message that says why and who to ask for access. Never a blank screen, never a grey button without a reason.
The same button means the same for everybody: if two profiles share a label, they share an effect. If the effect changes per profile, the label changes or the functionality is split in two.
Data is also filtered by profile: whoever sees the list sees the rows that correspond to them, not the whole list with the rows hidden in the browser.
The matrix and the user manual are updated in the same pending item as the functionality. A new functionality without a row in the matrix does not close.
Every list has four resolved states: with data, empty, loading and with error. The empty one distinguishes "there is nothing yet" from "your search found nothing".
While something takes time, it is visible that it is working and it can be cancelled if it is long. A button that answers nothing is complaint number one.
The error says what happened, what can be done and does not erase what was entered. Neither a technical code alone, nor an "an error occurred".
A screen has one evident main action; the rest are secondary and look like it.
Every destructive action asks for confirmation naming the affected object, and when it can be done it is undone instead of confirmed.
A form that fails keeps what was entered and marks the field with the problem, in the place of the field.
No action leaves the screen without an exit: after saving, deleting or cancelling, the person knows where they are and how to continue.
The interface speaks the language of the project glossary: the same object is called the same on the screen, in the manual and in the email. A synonym is a defect.
Everything can be done without a mouse and with a screen reader in the main flows; the focus is always visible and it does not get trapped.
States are not communicated by colour alone; every informative image has alternative text; texts are read at normal size without zoom.
Every pending item that touches a screen delivers the real screenshot of the test environment, and the owner looks at it before closing. The screenshot is not optional and it is not a mock-up.

adapters.what: Layer 2 of Annex H: per frontend family, with what each rule is measured and with which default threshold. Whatever the annex declares is here; whatever the annex leaves to the project is published as UNDECLARED, never with an invented value. The tool names in the example of the annex (section 7) are illustrative and are therefore NOT copied here: a tool named in this data would read as a default, and it is not one.

layers.1: agnostic core: the statement of the rule, the same in every project, not negotiable
layers.2: adapter per frontend family: with what it is measured and with which starting threshold
layers.3: project decisions: the concrete thresholds and the exceptions, declared by the owner and never by the agent

annex_columns.note: The table says with what each of those six is measured in each family. The text of every cell lives only in the annex: what goes here is the pointer.

measured_by.in: a single configuration file per project
measured_by.note: The annex shows the SHAPE of the file, not final values. An installation that takes those names as defaults is inventing layer 2.

thresholds.note: starting value of the core; the project may declare its own
starting value of the core; the project may declare its own
the annex requires the limit to be declared and does not fix the number: with no declaration it is reported as an undeclared threshold

thresholds.declared_by: the ratchet, over what is measured
thresholds.note: the zero in the example is deliberate: the floor is the number of today, not a factory value

thresholds.declared_by: the owner, once the project has real users
thresholds.note: the zero in the example is deliberate

adapters.undeclared_threshold: it is reported as an undeclared threshold. No approximating, no silent inheriting and no inventing: the same rule as the sizing of the architecture step.

project_config.what: The shape of the per-project configuration that the gate reads (layer 3 of Annex H). It lives in the project, never inside a prompt (D-046), and these are the field names a consumer tool has to write and read. Declared here so no tool has to guess them.

fields.frontend: Id of the adapter family (see gates/adapters.json families).
fields.real_users: Boolean. Rules with applies_if real_users only run where it is true, and that is scope, not an exception.
fields.switches: One entry per rule group: true, or an object { on: false, reason, authorized_by, review_date }.
fields.switched_off: List of individual rules switched off, each with the full record.
fields.thresholds: Declared values, by threshold id. Whatever is not here is reported as undeclared, never invented.
fields.tools: Tool names and versions actually used, for the ruleset fingerprint.

project_config.without_record: red, and the ruleset is invalid: the scoreboard emits no figures at all (D-046, D-047).
